column2: we drop all the range items (BTRFS_DIR_LOG_INDEX_KEY key

column1: type). This is because we will process all leaves in the subvolume's tree
that were changed in the current transaction and then add range items for
covering new dir index items and deleted dir index items
cover now a larger range than before.
We used to fail if we tried to insert a range item key that already
exists
column2: so we dropped all range items to avoid failing. However nowadays

column1: since commit 750ee454908e90 (""btrfs: fix assertion failure when logging
directory key range item"")
column2: we simply update any range item that already

column1: exists
column2: increasing its range's last dir index if needed. Since the range

column1: covered by a range item can never decrease
column2: due to the fact that dir index

column1: values come from a monotonically increasing counter and are never reused
we can stop dropping all range items before we start logging a directory.
By not dropping the items we can avoid having occasional tree rebalance
operations.
This will also be needed for an incoming change where we start logging
delayed items directly
